metadata.topic: WALKER - FIRST 3D ASSETS WITH THE BLENDER MCP
metadata.audience: Course reviewers reading an Assignment 3 Blender-to-Godot pass
metadata.greeting_note: hello lexicon: Sawubona (Zulu), one word, the Liam persona budget. Wagwan is Bear's alone and is not used.

beats.narration_text: Sawubona. The prompt on screen is a reconstruction, not a transcript. Assignment three asks for three simple 3D assets, built with Claude through the Blender MCP, and shown together in Godot. The game is the same dungeon the last film took apart. The assets are three things it already draws in code.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a cyber-ninja in a torchlit dungeon into three simple 3D assets I can put in Godot: the wall torch, the pop-up spike trap and the slime. Build them in my open Blender through the MCP, from basic shapes only, at the sizes my 2D level already uses.
output: every size taken from the 2D game

beats.narration_text: One correction before we start. Nothing here was generated. A 3D generator was available in the same add-on and the assignment forbids it, so the geometry is built: eleven primitives, placed and scaled by scripts you can read, two hundred and ten triangles for all three.

props.text:
Claude generated three assets.
Claude built them.

beats.narration_text: The trap is four shapes. The tooth count is not a choice: the 2D game's spike_count is the rect width over the pitch, twenty-four over eight, three. Pitch here is the width over that same count, so the 3D asset and the thing it stands for are built from one number.

beats.narration_text: There it is, from four sides. Fifty-four triangles. One point five metres wide and one metre tall, which is the level file's own trap rect. The teeth read as teeth from the side, and the top view shows the eight-sided cones the budget bought.

beats.narration_text: The slime missed its own brief by fifteen per cent. An icosphere is a faceted solid, and there is no ring of vertices on the plane it gets cut at, so a dome built at one point three seven five measured one point one seven. This measures the mesh after the cut and scales it to the number the brief promised.

props.title: Measure, then scale - not a magic constant
props.imageLabel: lines 98-109, verbatim - the file the MCP executed

notes.label: The quick fix, rejected
notes.value: multiplying by 1.174, a constant taken from one measurement

notes.label: Why that matters
notes.value: raising SUBDIV later would have moved it off the brief, silently

beats.role_note: RESULT. Real engine or session evidence, hashed in the ledger.
beats.narration_text: Every check passed on the one on the left. Correct size, origin on the floor, scale one. It also has a pointed top, and the 2D game draws a smooth dome. No assertion was going to catch that. Subdivision two, twenty more triangles, still inside the budget the brief wrote down.

beats.narration_text: This walks the imported scene and accumulates each node's local transform. The first version read global transform instead, from nodes a script in underscore init has not put in the tree yet. Every transform came back identity, and it reported a correct asset as sunk four hundred millimetres into the floor.

props.title: The check that was wrong before any asset was

notes.label: The giveaway
notes.value: 0.850 m tall and -0.425 m low: exactly the cone's local half-height

notes.label: The assignment's warning
notes.value: an agent's check can prove less than it claims

beats.role_note: RESULT. Real engine or session evidence, hashed in the ledger.
beats.narration_text: Headless, in Godot. Each asset's bounding box printed beside the number the brief predicted, which axis it stands along, its node scale, and how far its lowest point sits from the floor. Twelve measurements, no failures. What it cannot tell you is whether any of them looks like a torch.

props.imageLabel: headless output - the run's own stdout, not a transcription

notes.label: Exit code
notes.value: 0 on pass, 1 on any failure - the script quits itself

notes.label: What it does not show
notes.value: whether an asset reads, whether a face is missing, whether it suits

beats.role_note: RESULT. Real engine or session evidence, hashed in the ledger.
beats.narration_text: The assignment wants one change made by hand, with the mouse. The eyes were too small to read beside a player who is one point seven five metres, so I scaled them in the viewport. One frame carries the file name, the selected eye, its position to five decimals, and a scale of one, because the transform was applied afterwards.

beats.role_note: RESULT. Real engine or session evidence, hashed in the ledger.
beats.narration_text: A floor, one light, a camera, and the three assets one point nine metres apart. Each sits on the floor because each origin is at the centre of its underside. That is the brief's third prediction made into the scene's layout, where floating would be visible rather than merely measurable.

props.title: All three, in the running Godot scene
props.imageLabel: a frame from a real run of the scene, at game scale

notes.label: One light
notes.value: the DirectionalLight3D. The WorldEnvironment is ambient, not a second light

notes.label: Why ambient at all
notes.value: without it an unlit face reads as a hole and the human check fails

beats.narration_text: What this film can defend. Three assets, built not generated, every size traced to a line in the 2D game. Twelve automated measurements, no failures. Two revisions that no check asked for, because a person looked. And one human check, one sentence long, recorded as one sentence rather than dressed up.

props.artifactHeading: Built, measured, and what stayed unmeasured
artifactLines: Built: torch, spike trap, slime - 11 primitives, 210 triangles.
Generated: nothing. All six libraries and generators off.
Sizes: every one traced to the level file or a draw function.
The check was wrong before any asset was, and is recorded.
Revised twice on sight: the slime's shape and its eyes.
Human check: one sentence. Recorded as one sentence.
Not shown: the assets inside the 2D game. Not asked for yet.

beats.role_note: WALKER BOOKEND 4/4 - Your Turn. One bounded change, prediction first.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Give the torch a light. Predict the number before you run it: the 2D glow is sixteen nested discs with an outer radius of sixty pixels, which at sixteen pixels to the metre is three point seven five metres of reach. Then look, because the check measures geometry and a light is not geometry. Liam, signing off.

props.topic: WALKER - GIVE THE TORCH A LIGHT
props.command: In walker-ninja, add an OmniLight3D as a child of the Torch in scenes/asset_showcase.tscn, with a range derived from the 2D glow in _draw_torch. Write the predicted range in the commit message before you run it, then look at the frame.
props.runningText: predict the range first - then look
output: at 16 px = 1 m that is 3.75 m of reach
check_assets_3d.gd will not notice either way
